by_task.when: Wisconsin exemptions are allowable and valuing a motor vehicle under Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(g).
by_task.procedure: Value the § 815.18(3)(g) alternative at the lesser of the vehicle value and $16,000 for one debtor or $32,000 for two equal joint debtors, because unused § 815.18(3)(d) capacity may be added to the vehicle ceiling. Reduce that maximum only if the facts state that consumer-goods capacity was actually consumed.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not stop at the $4,000 base when the consumer-goods capacity is unused, double the ceiling for a single debtor, classify the vehicle separately under subsection (d), or apply these Wisconsin amounts to a Federal alternative.

operations.rationale: In all four sources, the actual parent valued the Wisconsin motor-vehicle alternative at only $4,000. The released targets instead use the vehicle ceiling plus unused § 815.18(3)(d) capacity: up to $16,000 for one debtor and $32,000 for two joint debtors, capped by vehicle value. A separate EV-only skill avoids changing the already committed Wisconsin EC boundary or contaminating Federal valuation.
